title: The popularity of kosher food
titleChinese: 引领饮食潮流的犹太洁食
paragraphs: Have you ever eaten kosher food? That's food which conforms to the Jewish dietary regulations of kashrut. These regulations forbid consuming pork or shellfish of any kind, for example. Meat from other animals, such as cows and lamb, are okay provided restrictions are met. But they must be slaughtered according to set guidelines. All kosher rulings are overseen by trained rabbis from a kosher certification agency. They inspect, uphold and grant rights to label a food kosher. Ordinarily, kosher food is associated with the Jewish faith, but it's becoming very popular among non-Jews too.

According to the Jewish telegraphic agency, as of 2018 there were approximately 7.5 million Jews in the United States. But, according to a study by the Quartz business news website, 41% of all packaged foodstuffs there are certified kosher. In fact, the global kosher food market is predicted to rise to $60 billion in annual sales by 2025 - according to PR Newswire, a press release distribution network.

Why might this be? One reason is the possible perception that kosher food is cleaner or healthier. Another is the guarantee that certain allergens, such as shellfish, will definitely not be permitted. And its protocols mean anyone seeking to avoid certain ingredients like gelatine, can do so.

“It appeals to a more health-conscious consumer,” says Menachem Lubinsky, CEO of Lubicom. They're the organiser of "Kosherfest", a two-day event that advertises itself as 'the world's largest and most attended kosher-certified products trade show'. In 2019, at its 31st event in New Jersey, attendance was up from the previous year by 800, and 300 new products were on display. In addition, non-Jewish-owned companies from places such as Pakistan, South Korea and Italy were in attendance.

So keep your eyes peeled for an authorised kosher trademark the next time you're food shopping. Based on their popularity to date, it might not be long before we're all eating a little something kosher.

vocabulary.entry: kosher /ˈkəʊʃə(r)/ adj. 符合犹太教饮食规定的；洁食的
vocabulary.example: We bought some kosher sausages for the party.
vocabulary.translation: 我们为派对买了一些洁食香肠。

vocabulary.entry: dietary regulations /ˈdaɪətəri ˌreɡjuˈleɪʃnz/ 饮食规定；膳食条例
vocabulary.example: The school has strict dietary regulations for students with allergies.
vocabulary.translation: 该校针对过敏学生制定了严格的饮食规定。

vocabulary.entry: kashrut /ˈkæʃruːt/ n. 犹太教饮食教规
vocabulary.example: Kashrut specifies which foods Jewish people can eat.
vocabulary.translation: 犹太教饮食教规明确规定了犹太人可以食用的食物种类。

vocabulary.entry: shellfish /ˈʃelfɪʃ/ n. 贝类海鲜（如虾、蟹、牡蛎等）
vocabulary.example: She is allergic to shellfish and can't eat any shrimp or crabs.
vocabulary.translation: 她对贝类海鲜过敏，一点虾和蟹都不能吃。

vocabulary.example: The animals must be slaughtered humanely according to the law.
vocabulary.translation: 根据法律规定，宰杀动物时必须遵循人道原则。

vocabulary.entry: guidelines /ˈɡaɪdlaɪnz/ n. 指导方针；行为准则
vocabulary.example: The government issued new guidelines on environmental protection.
vocabulary.translation: 政府出台了新的环境保护指导方针。

vocabulary.entry: rabbi /ˈræbaɪ/ n. 拉比（犹太教神职人员）
vocabulary.example: The rabbi will explain the religious traditions to the visitors.
vocabulary.translation: 这位拉比会向访客讲解相关宗教传统。

vocabulary.entry: trade show /treɪd ʃəʊ/ 贸易展览会
vocabulary.example: He will showcase his new products at an international trade show.
vocabulary.translation: 他将在一场国际贸易展览会上展示自己的新产品。

vocabulary.entry: uphold /ʌpˈhəʊld/ v. 维护；坚持（原则、法律等）
vocabulary.example: The court's job is to uphold the law and protect people's rights.
vocabulary.translation: 法庭的职责是维护法律，保障人们的权利。

vocabulary.entry: Jewish faith /ˈdʒuːɪʃ feɪθ/ 犹太教信仰
vocabulary.example: The Jewish faith has a long and rich history.
vocabulary.translation: 犹太教信仰有着悠久且丰富的历史。

vocabulary.example: The project will take approximately three months to complete.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目大约需要三个月才能完成。

vocabulary.entry: packaged foodstuffs /ˈpækɪdʒd ˈfuːdstʌfs/ 包装食品
vocabulary.example: The supermarket offers a wide range of packaged foodstuffs.
vocabulary.translation: 这家超市供应种类繁多的包装食品。

vocabulary.entry: attendance /əˈtendəns/ n. 出席人数；参加人数
vocabulary.example: The attendance at the concert was much higher than expected.
vocabulary.translation: 这场音乐会的出席人数远超预期。

vocabulary.entry: annual sales /ˈænjuəl seɪlz/ 年销售额
vocabulary.example: The company's annual sales exceeded one billion dollars last year.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司去年的年销售额突破了十亿美元。

vocabulary.example: People's perception of success varies from person to person.
vocabulary.translation: 人们对成功的看法因人而异。

vocabulary.example: Peanuts are a common allergen for many children.
vocabulary.translation: 花生是许多儿童常见的过敏原。

vocabulary.entry: protocol /ˈprəʊtəkɒl/ n. 规程；行为规范
vocabulary.example: The meeting followed a strict protocol from start to finish.
vocabulary.translation: 这场会议自始至终都遵循着严格的规程。

vocabulary.entry: gelatine /ˈdʒelətiːn/ n. 明胶（用于制作食品、药品等）
vocabulary.example: Gelatine is often used to make jellies and desserts.
vocabulary.translation: 明胶常被用来制作果冻和甜点。

vocabulary.entry: health-conscious /ˈhelθ ˈkɒnʃəs/ adj. 注重健康的
vocabulary.example: Health-conscious consumers prefer organic food over processed food.
vocabulary.translation: 注重健康的消费者更青睐有机食品，而非加工食品。

sentences.english: Ordinarily, kosher food is associated with the Jewish faith, but it's becoming very popular among non-Jews too.
sentences.chinese: 通常来说，洁食都与犹太教信仰挂钩，但如今它在非犹太人中也变得十分受欢迎。

sentences.english: But, according to a study by the Quartz business news website, 41% of all packaged foodstuffs there are certified kosher.

出现这种情况的原因是什么呢？

sentences.english: One reason is the possible perception that kosher food is cleaner or healthier.

sentences.english: Another is the guarantee that certain allergens, such as shellfish, will definitely not be permitted.
sentences.chinese: 其二，洁食能保证绝对不含某些过敏原，比如贝类海鲜。

sentences.english: And its protocols mean anyone seeking to avoid certain ingredients like gelatine, can do so.
sentences.chinese: 此外，洁食的生产流程规定，也能让那些想要避开明胶等特定成分的人放心食用。

sentences.english: “It appeals to a more health-conscious consumer,” says Menachem Lubinsky, CEO of Lubicom.
sentences.chinese: 卢比康公司首席执行官梅纳赫姆·卢宾斯基表示：“洁食对那些更注重健康的消费者很有吸引力。”

sentences.english: They're the organiser of "Kosherfest", a two-day event that advertises itself as 'the world's largest and most attended kosher-certified products trade show'.
sentences.chinese: 该公司是“洁食博览会”的主办方，这场为期两天的展会自称是“全球规模最大、参展人数最多的洁食认证产品贸易展”。

sentences.chinese: 所以下次采购食品的时候，不妨留意一下官方认证的洁食标识。

sentences.chinese: 从洁食当下的受欢迎程度来看，要不了多久，我们每个人或许都会吃上一些洁食。
